messages:
linus: Heads up — after the v2026.2 roll to full in eu1, the needle probe (canary slice) stopped reporting metrics ~12:03 UTC. p95 latency jumped from 220ms to 2.8s, then samples dropped to 0/5. Anyone seeing matching alerts?

deploy-bot: deploy v2026.2 -> eu1 canary completed 1719876500. smoke-synth: failing 3/5. Autocancel: false.

anya: looking at the probe logs now. pulling trace for request id 0x9f... Might be the probe instance hitting connection errors to kv-cache.

maria: are we seeing 5xx from inference proxy or just timeouts?

linus: no 5xx, probe timeouts with connect errors. curl from probe host to kv-service times out. `curl -v http://kv-eu1.internal/health` hangs.

kevin: I see transient network flap on host pool eu1-gpu-6 in host metrics. Host-level NIC errors at 12:01-12:05. SRE engaged.

oncall-bot: Pager duty: sre-team, severity 3. Incident created: INC-2026-199

anya: quick suggestion — can we pin canary routing off eu1 for the smoke probe while SRE investigates? That'll keep the main traffic healthy.

maria: +1 pin the smokeprobe route to eu1-secondary for now, and mark canary as paused. Which route key to change?

linus: I'll open a quick routing pin: change `smokeprobe/eu1` -> `eu1-b` (fallback region) and set rollout.pause=true for canary. Doing now.

linus: (applied) routing pin pushed. smokeprobe now hitting eu1-b — initial samples returning, p95 back to ~210ms.

kevin: SRE will continue host remediation. If we want to progressively unpin, we can re-enable canary after host patch and 30m stable probe.

maria: also adding brief note to release notes: 'v2026.2: temporary routing pin of smokeprobe in eu1 due to host NIC errors; no customer-facing failures.'

linus: Agreed. Can someone add to the change window doc that we paused canary at 12:04 UTC and pinned probes?

anya: I'll update the change window. Also scheduling a quick postmortem if host flaps persist.

maria: thanks — closing thread once SRE confirms. :thumbsup:
